Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Utilities Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, VP Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Utilities' Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Regulatory Officer; and Maria Lopez, Chief Communications Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Reliability metrics including SAIDI and SAIFI, alongside strong system performance.
    2. Progress in grid modernization and smart grid initiatives.
    3. Positive updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes.
    4. Excellent generation fleet performance and availability.
    5. Proactive management of regulatory lag and related mitigation strategies.
    6. Robust earnings per share performance and its key drivers.
    7. Favorable rate base growth outlook and underlying assumptions.
    8. Effective O&M expense management initiatives yielding efficiency gains.

Let me provide some more detail on these eight key aspects. Starting with reliability, our SAIDI improved 12% year-over-year to 128.4 minutes, with SAIFI down 8% to 1.12, beating targets despite severe weather—more from Mike shortly. On grid modernization, we've deployed $650 million this year in smart meters and automation, cutting outages significantly—Elena will expand. Regulatory rate cases saw key settlements, like our California GRC approving most of a $1.2 billion ask—Robert has details. Generation fleet hit 93.2% EAF, up 150 bps—Mike on ops. We're mitigating regulatory lag through riders and PBR, limiting impact to $185 million—Sarah will cover financially. EPS came in at $1.47, up 12%, driven by volumes and rates. Rate base grew 6.2% to $26.4 billion, guiding 6-7.5% CAGR. And O&M down 7.2% through predictive tech. We've also integrated our acquired 200 MW Florida solar portfolio seamlessly, advanced our Grid Resilience Program, secured positive outcomes in Illinois, and boosted community engagement in Atlanta.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss the financials.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.47 and revenue of $2.8 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Let me walk you through our EPS performance and drivers first. This $1.47 adjusted EPS marks a robust 12% increase year-over-year from $1.31, exceeding our guidance of $1.35 to $1.42 and Wall Street consensus of $1.41 by 4%. Year-to-date, it's $2.91, up 11%. Excluding a $0.08 gain from our Ohio coal sale and a $0.05 Texas disallowance, core drivers included 9% revenue growth to $2.8 billion from higher volumes—retail up 6% to 28.5 million MWh on 15% above-normal cooling degrees—and industrial strength from 1.2 GW data center PPAs. Regulated T&D added $450 million, up 7%, with PJM and ERCOT riders contributing $0.03 and $0.04 per share. Fleet availability at 93.2% added $0.09, O&M up just 3% thanks to digital twins, fuel hedges at $3.20/MMBtu, and capacity auctions yielding $120 million, up 25%. Renewables at 22% output with IRA credits added $0.06. Balanced regionally, with Northeast leading. This underpins full-year guidance of $5.85-$6.05, 10-14% growth.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $650 million, primarily focused on grid modernization and reliability enhancements. On rate base growth outlook, it stood at $26.4 billion end-Q3, up 6.2% YoY. We guide 6-7.5% CAGR to $36-38 billion by 2028 on $18-20 billion capex—60% T&D like HTLS lines and automation, 25% clean energy including 1.2 GW solar-storage, 15% resilience. Drivers: T&D 40%, gen transition 30%, load growth 20% from EVs/data centers. Regional: 7-8% Southeast, 6% Texas, 4-5% Midwest. Assumptions: 100% CWIP recovery, 95% execution, 2-3% GDP, 3.5% load growth, inflation 2.5%. Sensitivities include rates, FERC; upside from IRA, PPAs. This supports 7-9% EPS CAGR.

Turning to O&M management, we cut expenses 7.2% YoY to $285 million or $19/MWh, on track for $120 million full-year savings. Thermal predictive maintenance via GE Vernova reduced outages 22%, saving $28 million; Midwest retrofits $15 million; renewables drone inspections down 11% to $22k/MW; T&D fault prediction saved $10 million. Workforce cross-training cut overtime 18%, procurement 12% savings. Aligns with Efficient Growth 2030 for 10-12% productivity.

On regulatory lag, averaging 10-12 months, it dragged $185 million or 2.2% ROE in 2023 from $450 million unplanned capex. Mitigations: riders like $250 million MISO transmission approved 100%; decoupling stabilizing revenues; trackers 40% capex; digital ADMS improving forecasts 25%; BESS/VPPs earning credits. Filing full GRC Q1 2025 for $1.2 billion. Expect 1.5% ROE impact 2025. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate 6-8% EPS growth in 2025.

Mike Thornton: Thank you, Sarah. Let me provide an update on the operational front, starting with generation fleet performance. Our diversified 25 GW fleet across PJM, MISO, ERCOT achieved 93.2% EAF in Q3, up 150 bps YoY to beat 92% target, with EFOR down to 4.1% and 42.2 TWh output at 68% capacity factor. Thermal CCGTs at 95.8% EAF, heat rate 6,450 Btu/kWh via 20% H2 blending; coal 88% amid retirements; nuclear 93.5% CF with digital twins; renewables 38% wind/27% solar CF, BESS 95% efficiency. Regional highs in ERCOT at 97%. $1.2 billion 2024 capex, AI cutting outages 25%. Guide FY24 92.5-93.5% EAF.

We're also seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbines due to ADMS implementation, resulting in a 22% increase in output. Outage rates down 18%. On reliability metrics and system performance, we've transformed via our $1.2 billion Grid Resilience Program. FY23 SAIDI 128.4 minutes, 12% better than 145.9, top 20% EEI peers; SAIFI 1.12, down 8%. Ex-EME: 89.2/0.78. 3-year CAGR -14%/-9% SAIDI/SAIFI. Midwest 142 min SAIDI from storms; Southeast 98 min, undergrounding 45%. Drivers: weather 47%, veg mgmt down to 22% via LiDAR, aging infra 18% cut 15%. Initiatives: $450M capex—ADMS 85% rollout shaving 22 min restoration, 1.1M AMI/FPIs 92% coverage, drones 12k miles, SF6-free breakers, 5 resilience hubs mitigating 14k customer-minutes. Ties to Illinois rate case $800M undergrounding, 3:1 BCR. 2024 targets: SAIDI <120, SAIFI 1.05, $500M capex, AI predictive 85%.

David Patel: Thank you, Mike. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery energy storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the Texas ERCOT market.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, David. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. Our $2.8 billion program, $650 million in FY23 up 25%, drives $120 million rate base growth, 50 bps ROE boost. AMI: 4.2M smart meters, 92% coverage, TOU shifting 15% peak, $45M revenue. FLISR on 65% feeders, SAIDI -22% to 85 min, SAIFI -18% to 0.95; Q4 restored 250k customers, saved $12M. Northeast $180M sensors/microgrids 1.2 GW BESS; Midwest $220M smart inverters 800 MW. Cyber: NERC CIP-013, zero-trust Palo Alto, Dragos AI mitigated probes. O&M -28% predictive IoT/Palantir. 2024 $850M capex, EV pilots. Synergies: peakers $75M ancillaries, VPPs 300 MW. 2.5x ROI. We've recently deployed zero-trust architecture from Palo Alto Networks to enhance defenses against cyber threats. We are also piloting FLISR in Midwest substations.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Elena. On the regulatory front, we received approval for our general rate case in Illinois. This will allow us to recover $1.2 billion in revenue requirement over three years. Across jurisdictions: California GRC settlement $1.02B/10.35% ROE, wildfire/1.2 GW BESS; Texas TCOS 92% of $850M/10.15% ROE; NY biennial interim $420M/9.75% ROE PBR; FERC MISO $220M/10.2% ROE. Upcoming: Texas storage, CA O&M. 95% 2025 revenues regulated.

Maria Lopez: Thank you, Robert. We are pleased to announce that our community outreach program in Atlanta has resulted in a 25% increase in positive sentiment towards Apex Utilities.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Sarah, Mike, David, Elena, Robert, and Maria. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Davis with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Davis: Good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your reliability metrics this quarter—specifically SAIDI and SAIFI—and how they're tying into broader system performance. With the severe weather across your footprint, can you walk us through the trends, drivers, and what your capex initiatives are doing to shore this up?

Mark Thompson: Great question, John, and one we're hearing a lot. I'll turn this over to our COO, Mike Thornton, who's leading our reliability efforts.

Mike Thornton: Thanks, Mark, and good morning, John. Let me give you a comprehensive update on our reliability metrics—focusing on SAIDI and SAIFI—as well as system performance trends. I'll cover highlights, regional variances, drivers, initiatives, and forward insights, tying into rate cases and top-quartile 92% J.D. Power scores.

Headline FY23: SAIDI 128.4 minutes, 12% YoY improvement from 145.9, beating 135 target, top 20% EEI like Duke/Xcel. SAIFI 1.12, down 8% from 1.22. Ex-EME (Q2 tornadoes): SAIDI 89.2, SAIFI 0.78, NextEra FPL level. 3-year: 28% SAIDI drop from 179 baseline, -14% CAGR; SAIFI -9% CAGR vs. US median 160 min.

Regions, 1.2M customers Midwest/Southeast: Midwest (60% load) SAIDI 142 min/SAIFI 1.35 from 17 storms, rural 60%; urban <100. Southeast (40%) 98/0.72, undergrounding 45% metro Atlanta limited Idalia to 12% customers.

Drivers: weather 47%, veg mgmt 22% (down 31%, LiDAR 4-yr cycle), aging 18% (relay upgrades -15%), renewables/EV flicker <2% via VAR. Initiatives $450M/28% grid spend: GE ADMS 6.0 85% substations FLISR -22 min restoration; 1.1M Landis+Gyr AMI/FPIs 92% coverage -40% detect; Trimble drones 12k miles/18k risks; ABB SF6-free 50 substations -25% fails; 5 Alabama hubs 5MW/20MWh Fluence -14k min Idalia.

Regulatory: Illinois case $800M 5-yr undergrounding 55% by 2028, 3:1 BCR dodging $0.50/kWh PIPP; ARPU +5% $142/mo. 2024: SAIDI <120/SAIFI 1.05, $500M capex. Risks La Niña/2.5 GW DER; mitigators Siemens AI 85% forecast, drone swarms.

In sum, this positions us top-tier for EV/data center/renewables load. Happy for follow-ups.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: What is your outlook for rate base growth and key assumptions?

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, Lisa. As detailed earlier, rate base at $26.4B up 6.2% YoY, guiding 6-7.5% CAGR to $36-38B by 2028 on $18-20B capex: 60% T&D (HTLS $1.2B, substations $800M), 25% clean (1.2 GW solar-storage, 1.5 GWh BESS), 15% resilience. T&D 40%, gen 30% AFUDC 75-100 bps, load 20%. Southeast 7-8%, Texas 6%, Midwest/Northeast 4-5%. Assumptions: CWIP 100%/80% jurs, 9-mo lags, 95% execution, 5-7% supply premiums, 55% equity WACC 6.2%, 2-3% GDP/3.5% load/2.5% inflation, gas $3-3.5. Risks 50 bps rate hike -20 bps; upside IRA/1 GW PPAs. Underpins 7-9% EPS CAGR.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly: How are you mitigating risks related to regulatory lag?

Mike Thornton: Thanks, Tom. While Sarah touched on it, regulatory lag—the mismatch between capex and rate recovery—averaged 10-12 months, $185M drag/2.2% ROE in 2023 from $450M unplanned. Illinois 14 mo, Indiana <8 mo, PJM queues 18-24 mo. Mitigations shielded 65%/$120M: proactive filings—$250M MISO rider 100%/10.5% ROE, $75M EV Ohio, $60M MI storm; decoupling 85% opex; PBR 20% revenues to SAIDI/DER; trackers 40% incl. pension/env CCUS 45Q; securitization $300M MI bonds 4.2%. Digital: ADMS/ADER 25% forecast, 500 MW BESS GE, VPPs 100 MW $15M. Analytics Brattle Monte Carlo to 6 mo by 2027, RTO advocacy FERC 1920. 2025 1.5% impact, $3.5-3.8B capex 70% AFUDC, 6-8% EPS.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Grant with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Grant: What is the anticipated impact of recent regulatory rate case outcomes on your earnings?

Robert Kline: Thanks, Emily. Our multi-state filings validate strategy. California GRC $1.2B ask, settled $1.02B/10.35% ROE 52/48 structure, 85% recovery incl. $450M wildfire AB1054/decoupling 28% solar; $0.22 2025 EPS, bills +4.2%. Texas TCOS $850M/92% 10.15% ROE formulaic, 300 mi 345kV/1.5 GW renewables. NY biennial $650M interim $420M/9.75% PBR 20% to reliability/decarb CLCPA. FERC MISO true-up $220M/10.2%+50 bps. Next: TX storage DOE grants, CA $500M O&M SF6. Trends ROE 9.8%, 95% 2025 revenues regulated, EPS visibility.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Mark Thompson for closing remarks.

Mark Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Utilities for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Utilities.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
